questions.stem: A bag contains 4 red, 5 green, and 6 blue balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is green?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Total balls = 4+5+6 = 15. P(green) = 5/15 = 1/3.

questions.stem: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of drawing a black king?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Black kings = king of spades + king of clubs = 2 cards. P = 2/52 = 1/26.

questions.stem: A single fair die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Outcomes > 4: {5, 6} = 2. Total outcomes = 6. P = 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 white and 4 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. Find the probability that one is white and one is black.
questions.explanation: A is correct. Favourable ways = C(5,1) × C(4,1) = 5 × 4 = 20. Total ways = C(9,2) = 36. P = 20/36 = 5/9.

questions.stem: P(A) = 2/5 and P(B) = 1/3. A and B are independent events. Find P(A and B).
questions.explanation: A is correct. For independent events, P(A∩B) = P(A) × P(B) = 2/5 × 1/3 = 2/15.

A letter is chosen at random from the word 'STATISTICS'. What is the probability that it is a vowel?
questions.explanation: B is correct. STATISTICS: S,T,A,T,I,S,T,I,C,S = 10 letters. Vowels: A(1), I(2) = 3 vowels. P = 3/10.

questions.stem: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 100. What is the probability that it is a perfect square?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Perfect squares from 1 to 100: 1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100 = 10 numbers. P = 10/100 = 1/10.

questions.stem: A speaks truth 3/4 of the time and B speaks truth 4/5 of the time. What is the probability that they contradict each other on the same fact?
questions.explanation: A is correct. They contradict when one tells truth and the other lies. P = P(A true)×P(B lies) + P(A lies)×P(B true) = (3/4)(1/5) + (1/4)(4/5) = 3/20 + 4/20 = 7/20.

questions.stem: Three unbiased coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting at least 2 heads?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Sample space = 2³ = 8. Exactly 2H: HHT, HTH, THH = 3 outcomes. Exactly 3H: HHH = 1. Total favourable = 4. P = 4/8 = 1/2.
